extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators applying for ERC grants and their host institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards for preparing and submitting ERC Starting, Consolidator, Advanced and Proof of Concept grant proposals, including required proposal elements, PI track record expectations, time-commitment rules, eligibility and assessment criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence as the sole evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For all ERC frontier research grants, excellence is the sole criterion of evaluation, applied to both (a) the ground‑breaking nature, ambition and feasibility of the research project; and (b) the intellectual capacity, creativity and commitment of the Principal Investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During evaluation the PI's career phase, breaks, unconventional career paths and benchmark expectations (including minimum working time in EU/Associated Country and on the ERC project) should be taken into account. Excellence applies across Starting, Consolidator and Advanced grant types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research project — Ground‑breaking nature, ambition and potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent does the proposed research address important challenges; are the objectives ambitious and beyond the state of the art (e.g. novel concepts, cross‑disciplinary development); and to what extent is the proposed research high risk/high gain?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At step 1 the Extended Synopsis must present all essential information about ground‑breaking nature and feasibility because the full scientific proposal is not assessed at step 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research project — Scientific approach and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess feasibility given the high risk/high gain nature (from the Extended Synopsis); evaluate whether the research methodology is appropriate (from the full Scientific Proposal); whether the proposal involves development of novel methodology; and whether proposed timescales and resources are necessary and properly justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feasibility judgments at step 1 are based on the Extended Synopsis; full methodological assessment uses the complete Scientific Proposal at step 2. Timelines and resource justifications must be explicit in the full proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — Intellectual capacity and creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent has the PI demonstrated the ability to propose and conduct ground‑breaking research, evidence of creative independent thinking, and achievements beyond the state of the art?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Advanced Grants, evidence of sound leadership in the training and advancement of young scientists is also considered. Achievements should be presented in the CV and Track Record sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — Commitment and required time allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI must demonstrate willingness to devote a significant amount of time to the project and to spend a minimum portion of total working time in an EU Member State or Associated Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimums specified: Starting Grants — min 50% of total working time on the project; Consolidator Grants — min 40% on the project and min 50% working time in EU/Associated Country; Advanced Grants — min 30% on the project and min 50% working time in EU/Associated Country. PIs must ensure presence and sufficient time commitment throughout the project. Time commitment will be monitored and non‑compliance may lead to grant reduction, suspension or termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten‑year Track Record — required items to list
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Track Record the applicant should list up to ten representative publications from the last ten years as main author (or joint author where alphabetic order is norm) including citation counts (excluding self‑citations) and, as applicable: research monographs and translations, granted patents, invited presentations to peer‑reviewed international conferences/advanced schools, research expeditions led, organisation of international conferences (steering/organising committee), prizes/awards/academy memberships, contributions to early careers of excellent researchers, and examples of leadership in industrial innovation or design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the PI chooses, achievements older than ten years can be considered in specified circumstances (e.g. documented leave for maternity/paternity/long‑term illness/clinical qualification/national service) — extensions must be highlighted in the CV with documented evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant — illustrative benchmarks of an exceptional record
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Grant PIs are expected to be established research leaders with significant achievements in the last 10 years, typically matching one or more benchmarks such as: 10 publications as senior author in major international journals/conference proceedings; 3 major research monographs (at least one translated); 5 granted patents; 10 invited presentations at well‑established international conferences/advanced schools; 3 research expeditions led; 3 well‑established international conferences organised (steering/organising committee); international recognition through prizes/awards or academy memberships; major contributions to launching careers; recognised leadership in industrial innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are field‑dependent benchmarks; absence of such a record makes success unlikely. Alternative benchmarks may be considered individually or in combination as indicative of an exceptional record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal structure and strict page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete proposal must contain specified elements with strict page limits: Extended Synopsis (5 pages), Scientific Proposal (15 pages), Curriculum Vitae (2 pages), Track Record (2 pages), plus Host Institution Binding Statement, Ethics Review Table and supporting documentation (e.g., PhD record for Starting/Consolidator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page limits will be applied strictly; only material within the limits will be evaluated. Peer reviewers are under no obligation to read beyond the limits. For Proof of Concept proposals a strict 7‑page limit applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution Binding Statement of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution must provide a binding statement confirming its association with and support for the project and that the conditions of independence are already fulfilled or will be provided to the PI if the application is successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals missing this institutional statement may be declared ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and allocation rules for Proof of Concept (PoC) grants
rubrics_metrics.description: PoC Grants are available only to PIs of ERC frontier research projects that are ongoing or ended less than 12 months before the call opening date; proposals must draw substantially on ERC‑funded research; more than one PoC may be awarded per ERC project but only one PoC may be running at any time for the same ERC project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institution must engage the PI for at least the duration of the PoC project and be established in a Member State or Associated Country (or allowed entity types). Proposals out of scope are only declared ineligible in clear‑cut cases; in doubtful cases peer review may proceed pending eligibility committee decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Concept — maximum grant size, duration and eligible costs
rubrics_metrics.description: PoC grants: up to EUR 150,000 for up to 18 months (ERC expects normally completion within 12 months); reimbursement up to 100% of eligible direct costs plus flat‑rate indirect costs at 25% of eligible direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must fully justify the funding requested based on estimation of actual costs. Extensions beyond 18 months are exceptional. Costs excluded from the flat‑rate indirect calculation include subcontracting direct costs and resources provided by third parties not used on the host premises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Concept — evaluation criteria (three criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: PoC proposals are evaluated against: (1) Excellence (innovation potential) — does the activity move research outputs towards commercial or social innovation; (2) Impact — expected economic/societal benefits, identification of customers/end‑users, plans for commercialization or social benefit generation, analysis of distinctiveness vs existing solutions, confirmation/testing plans, IPR clarification and partner contacts; (3) Quality and efficiency of implementation — reasonable plan of activities against objectives, project management including risk/contingency planning, qualified personnel, and budget necessity and justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers evaluate each criterion on a pass/fail basis. A proposal must receive a pass by a majority of reviewers on all three criteria to be considered for funding. If budget is insufficient, passing proposals are ranked by reviewer marks; panels may meet to establish priority among equally ranked proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation procedure and two‑step review for frontier grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Full proposal submission followed by two‑step evaluation: Step 1 assesses the Extended Synopsis, PI Track Record and CV (not the full Scientific Proposal); Step 2 assesses the complete retained proposals including the full Scientific Proposal. Allocation to panels is based on the applicant's expressed preference; panels may request additional reviews or remote experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are retained to step 2 based on step 1 outcome and a budgetary cut‑off of three times the panel's indicative budget. Starting and Consolidator PIs retained to step 2 will be invited for an interview in Brussels. Applicants may request up to three persons not to act as evaluators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome categories and ranking at each evaluation step
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of each step proposals will be informed of outcome categories: Step 1 — (A) pass to step 2; (B) high quality but not pass to step 2; (C) not sufficient to pass to step 2. Step 2 — (A) fully meets excellence criterion and recommended for funding; (B) meets some but not all elements and will not be funded; (C) does not meet excellence criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final funding depends on ranking and available budget; applicants receive an evaluation report with ranking range. Restrictions on future submissions may apply depending on call rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required relation to ERC project for Proof of Concept
rubrics_metrics.description: PoC proposals must clearly demonstrate the relation between the idea to be taken to proof of concept and the ERC frontier research project from which it is substantially drawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial drawing on ERC‑funded research is required; the PoC funding is not aimed at extending the original research or primarily overcoming obstacles to practical application, but at early pre‑competitive steps to demonstrate innovation potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible/low‑priority project types
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects that are wholly or largely the collation and compilation of existing material into new databases, editions or collections are unlikely to constitute ground‑breaking or 'frontier' research and are therefore unlikely to be recommended for ERC funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While useful as resources, such projects rarely meet the ERC's excellence criterion for frontier research panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism detection and originality checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism detection software may be used to analyse proposals submitted to the ERC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure originality and proper citation; detected plagiarism may affect eligibility or evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal submission logistics and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are submitted electronically by the PI on behalf of the host institution; early registration and submission are strongly recommended. A PI may submit only one application per call. Applications must be complete and submitted before the call deadline; incomplete proposals may be declared ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information for Applicants published on ERC website and Participant Portal provides detailed completion instructions for electronic forms. For PoC calls, submissions are evaluated in three rounds with specific deadlines; a PI can submit one application per call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding justification and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: All funding requested is assessed during evaluation: amounts must be fully justified by estimation of the actual costs for the proposed activities and judged against the needs of the proposed activity before award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Advanced Grants an additional up to EUR 1,000,000 can be requested for start‑up costs, equipment or access to large facilities; such additional funding, being one‑off costs, is not subject to pro‑rata temporis reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to meet declared time commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: If the actual commitment is below the minimum levels set out for the grant type, or below the levels indicated in the proposal, appropriate measures may be taken, up to and including reduction of the grant and suspension or termination of grants in accordance with the grant agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time commitment is monitored throughout the project; applicants must specify percentages of total working time to be spent in EU/Associated Country and on the project in the Scientific Proposal.
